harmonicFunction: E (I) - Tonic chord establishing the grounding, resonant home key
A (IV) - Subdominant chord introducing melodic warmth and optimism
B (V) - Dominant chord propelling the phrase back to the tonic E with natural urgency

techniques.name: Dynamic 4/4 Acoustic Strumming
techniques.description: Driving down-up acoustic rhythm with steady eighth-note momentum and accented downbeats on beats 2 and 4

sequence: Keep right wrist loose and relaxed in continuous 4/4 motion
Accent the backbeat on 2 and 4 to lock in with the rhythm section
Let high E and B strings ring open freely during chord changes
tips: Use a medium pick (0.60mm to 0.73mm) for crisp acoustic projection
B7 (X-2-1-2-0-2) is an easier open alternative to the full B barre chord
Focus on smooth transitions between open A and B

sections.name: Intro
sections.description: Mark Seymour introduces the song with raw acoustic strums establishing the iconic four-bar cycle.
notes: Ringing open E chord letting low and high E strings ring out
Crisp dominant B chord leading into the verse

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: Storytelling verses backed by steady, relaxed acoustic strumming building dynamic energy.
sections.progression: E - A - B - E - E - A - B - E
notes: Maintain relaxed strumming without rushing the 104 BPM tempo
Leave room for the vocal line to breathe
Hit the bass notes cleanly on beat 1 of each measure

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: The soaring singalong chorus with open acoustic strumming at maximum dynamic volume.
sections.progression: E - A - B - E - E - A - B - E
notes: Dig in with full right-hand strumming strokes
Sing along at the top of your lungs
Keep the time solid and unwavering

sections.name: Scale Practice Exercise
sections.description: E major open scale exercise demonstrating notes connecting the E, A, and B chords.
notes: Connect open strings with fretted notes smoothly
Notice the leading tone D# resolving to tonic E

guitar.recommended: Maton EM100C or Cole Clark Fat Lady Acoustic
guitar.pickup: Under-saddle acoustic piezo with internal condenser blend

amp.recommended: Clean acoustic PA or AER Compact 60

beginner.title: Master the 3 Open Chords
steps: Practice open E major and open A major shapes
Learn B7 (X-2-1-2-0-2) as an accessible alternative to B barre
Strum through E - A - B - E at 80 BPM

intermediate.title: Solidify Barre Chords and Dynamics
steps: Practice dynamic control between quiet verses and loud choruses
Sing along while maintaining steady 4/4 acoustic strumming

advanced.title: Campfire Leadership & Performance
steps: Deliver the emotional storytelling nuance of Mark Seymour
Incorporate bass-note picking on beats 1 and 3
Lead a full acoustic singalong with crowd participation

commonMistakes: Rushing the tempo during the emotional chorus
Muting the high E and B strings on open A and B chords
Strumming with a stiff wrist causing fatigue
practiceRoutine: 2 minutes: Open chord finger warm-up across E, A, and B
5 minutes: Isolated B chord transition drill
5 minutes: Verse strumming pattern at 104 BPM
5 minutes: Chorus singing and playing integration
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 90 BPM for initial rhythm practice
Advance to target tempo of 104 BPM once chord changes are seamless
Practice with clicks on beats 2 and 4 to develop authentic groove
